title: mimid: PeerClient sends Host without the port when a peer's endpoints are on a non-default port
description: Found on the public B4 run (2026-11-13, tags t20261113203926 and t20261113203944) against our Haven at haven.reviewcommit.com, whose directory names wire endpoints at https://haven.reviewcommit.com:8443/... The namespace run could not show it (its URLs had no port). Wire capture (/var/log/mimid/ourhaven-8443.wire.log on the mimid host; copy in tools/interop/haven/live/out/public-<tag>/): every PeerClient request carries 'host: haven.reviewcommit.com', while curl to the same URLs sends 'Host: haven.reviewcommit.com:8443'. Cause: PeerClient::headers (crates/mimid-server/src/peer.rs ~L442-449) overrides Host with the bare peer domain, doc comment 'Host carries no port, which §4.1 says is ignored'. RFC 9112 §3.2 L437-441: 'If the target URI includes an authority component, then a client MUST send a field value for Host that is identical to that authority component'; RFC 9110 §7.2 L2414-2423 Host = uri-host [ ":" port ]. protocol-07 §4.1 L965-967 says the port component 'is ignored' by the receiver; it does not let the client drop it, and the target provider is still identified by the host part. Impact here: none (mimi-hubd does not read Host; all answers matched the namespace run). Risk: a front end that routes or checks Host:port (a reverse proxy on a shared IP, an HTTP/1.1 strict server) can misroute or refuse. Wrong reading: mimid. Fix: send the URL's authority (host[:port]) as Host, or let reqwest set it; the §4.1 target domain is then its host part. Note mimid-server is edited elsewhere: coordinate before changing peer.rs; a decision bead may be wanted since the current behaviour was deliberate.
